_comment: Every channel here must genuinely CC-BY-license its uploads on YouTube. research.py re-verifies status.license == 'creativeCommon' per video before use -- being listed here is a hint to search, not a trust shortcut. Add more by finding the channel's About page and confirming their license policy, not by assuming a conference is CC just because it's open source adjacent.

niche._env_suffix_comment: Suffix for the per-channel secrets (YT_REFRESH_TOKEN_<SUFFIX>, BUFFER_CHANNEL_ID_<SUFFIX>). Set separately from id so the niche can stay descriptive while the secrets are named after the channel they post to.
niche.name: CodeAZ Tech Shorts
niche.purpose: Clip CC-BY licensed tech videos from creators who already edit for attention -- B-roll, hooks, cuts -- because the clipper amplifies existing pacing and cannot invent it. Conference talks were tried first and produced unreadable slides in a letterboxed frame. Every clip credits and links the original video, creator and channel.

cc_channels.name: Mental Outlaw
cc_channels.note: Linux, privacy, security. Tight edit, opinionated delivery. 12 CC videos verified >=10min. The clip this niche was modelled on came from here.

cc_channels.name: Talking Sasquach
cc_channels.note: Flipper Zero, HackRF, hardware hacking and maker builds. Heavy B-roll. 21 CC videos verified.

niche._license_note: YouTube's 'Creative Commons - Attribution' dropdown grants CC BY 3.0. The CC flag covers what the uploader owns -- not third-party music, game footage or stock B-roll they licensed but cannot sublicense.
niche._layouts_comment: 'screencast' turns on OpenShorts' SCREENCAST_LAYOUT, which is off by default upstream. It measures how much of the frame WIDTH the on-screen content spans and routes those scenes to a stacked or full-width layout instead of the 9:16 tracking crop. Without it a screen recording that contains a face is classified TRACK and the crop keeps a centre strip -- which is how a 75s clip of a Reddit post shipped with every line of text sliced off both edges (youtu.be/UPH8HQ-kafc, 5-sep-2026).
niche._content_height_ratio_comment: GENERAL_CONTENT_HEIGHT_RATIO for the backend: how much of the frame height the content fills in the blurred-background layout, bought by CROPPING THE SIDES. There is a hard floor here and it is 0.316: a 16:9 source fills a 1080px-wide frame at 608px tall, and 608/1920 = 0.316. Every value above that discards width. Measured against reframe_v2's own filtergraph on a real source -- 0.6 (what shipped) keeps 53% of the width, 0.42 (upstream's default) keeps 75%, and both cut sentences in half on anything with text on screen. 0.31 sits under the floor so the max() in general_filtergraph pins the content to full width and nothing is ever cut. The cost is real and worth naming: at full width a 16:9 source is 32% of the frame height with blurred filler above and below, so the text is intact but small. That is the better failure. Cropping throws information away; small is still readable. If a clip looks like a thumbnail floating in soup, the fix is the SOURCE -- a video that is a static full-frame text page cannot be made good by any 9:16 layout -- not a higher ratio.
niche._cc_channels_removed: Removed after auditing what these channels publish against what their notes claimed. Humor Studios (UCQAbWYfvugVtd5sJ8lXDs4w): an AskReddit storytime channel, not the 'security/hacker story format' its note claimed; supplied six consecutive off-niche posts. CampusX (UCCWi3hpnq_Pe03nGxuS7isg): Hindi-language long-form lectures, the opposite of this niche's stated purpose. KristoferYee (UC_sHe3M2R5d_EWnv6Euaqlw): kept in the first pass on the reasoning that its build videos justified it, removed on 6-sep-2026 when the very next run cut 'Her Brother Won't Let Her Play on the Computer' into 'I realized I was a terrible brother' and 'The 1% rule that changed my life'. Its format is an emotional story with a PC in it, and a hardware word in the description is enough to pass a metadata filter. Run find_channels.py for replacements.
niche._topic_terms_comment: At least one of these must appear in a candidate's title, first 600 chars of description, or tags -- otherwise research.py skips it. Terms match on word boundaries, so 'ai' does not fire inside 'explain'. This is the check that was missing entirely: licence verification answers 'may we repost it' and the channel allowlist answers 'does this uploader license CC', and neither answers 'is it about our subject'.
niche._exclude_terms_comment: Checked BEFORE topic_terms and beats them: a storytime video whose description happens to say 'tech' is still a storytime video. Every one of the six off-niche posts from the 3-sep and 5-sep-2026 runs is rejected by this list, as is 'Linus Tech Tips Drama Explained' -- gossip about a tech company is not a tech video.
niche._allowed_languages_comment: Checked against snippet.defaultAudioLanguage / defaultLanguage. Topic keywords cannot see language: a Hindi machine-learning lecture matches 'machine learning' perfectly and is still unusable here -- that is how CampusX passed every check and got listed. Videos declaring no language are ALLOWED through: the field is optional and widely unset, so rejecting on absence would cost most of the pool to catch a few.
niche._clip_exclude_terms_comment: Applied by clip_verdict AFTER clipping, to the title/description/hook Gemini wrote for each clip -- on top of exclude_terms, which apply at both stages. This is the layer that catches what source metadata hides: a PC channel's video carries hardware words in its description and passes the research filter, while the 40 seconds actually cut from it is a sentimental story. Only exclusions run here, never topic_terms: a legitimate clip can open on a line that names no technology at all.
